options.text: An organism with a different set of genes from its parent
An organism that is genetically identical to another organism
An organism produced by sexual reproduction
An organism that has been genetically modified

questions.explanation: A clone is an organism that is genetically identical to another organism. Clones have the same DNA, though they may not be identical in appearance because environmental factors can also influence development.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of natural cloning?

options.text: Pollination of a flower
A cow giving birth to a calf
A bird laying eggs
Strawberry plants producing runners

questions.explanation: Strawberry plants producing runners is an example of natural cloning through asexual reproduction. The new plants that grow from runners are genetically identical to the parent plant. Other examples include bulbs and tubers.

questions.stem: In adult cell cloning (somatic cell nuclear transfer), the nucleus is removed from:

options.text: A sperm cell
A body cell of the organism to be cloned
A plant cell
A bacterial cell

questions.explanation: In adult cell cloning, the nucleus is taken from a body (somatic) cell of the organism to be cloned. This nucleus contains the complete set of DNA and is transferred into an enucleated egg cell to create a clone.

questions.stem: What must happen to the egg cell before the donor nucleus is inserted during adult cell cloning?

options.text: It must undergo meiosis
It must be frozen
It must be fertilised by a sperm cell
Its own nucleus must be removed (enucleated)

questions.explanation: The egg cell must be enucleated, meaning its own nucleus is removed. This ensures the clone's DNA comes entirely from the donor body cell. The egg cell still provides the cytoplasm and mitochondria needed for development.

questions.stem: What is a disadvantage of cloning animals?

options.text: It is too slow compared to natural reproduction
Cloned animals tend to age faster and may have health problems
It produces too much genetic variation
Cloned animals are always infertile

questions.explanation: Cloned animals often have health problems and may age prematurely. Dolly the sheep, the first cloned mammal, developed arthritis at a young age and was euthanised at age 6. There are also concerns about reduced genetic diversity.

questions.stem: How are plants commonly cloned artificially?

options.text: By nuclear transfer only
By crossing two different species
By pollination and seed collection
By taking cuttings or using tissue culture

questions.explanation: Plants can be cloned artificially by taking cuttings (sections of stem placed in soil to grow roots) or by tissue culture (growing new plants from small groups of cells on nutrient agar). Both methods produce genetically identical plants.

questions.stem: Why might cloning be useful in agriculture?

options.text: It allows rapid production of many identical plants with desirable characteristics
It increases genetic variation in crops
It reduces the need for sunlight
It makes plants resistant to all diseases

questions.explanation: Cloning is useful in agriculture because it allows farmers to rapidly produce many identical copies of plants with desirable characteristics, such as high yield or disease resistance, ensuring uniformity in the crop.
